frozen: 2026-10-25, before any of these results were computed (the seat counts per era were seen: 1,294 / 1,560 / 1,287 / 1,948 seats for 57.7 / 52.4 / 88.2 / 351.5 M people)
purpose: Three more Earth checks of the polity model with data already on disk: how county seats are spaced across 1,800 years of China, how far the drawn extent reaches from seats in later eras, and whether riding explains where a steppe polity's border with a farming state lay.

data.areas: Zheng & Wu (2026) ResearchArea, the same years: prefecture polygons with recorded population and area
data.polygons: Cliopatria v0.2.1: Xiongnu AD 2, the Turkic khaganate of AD 742 (as named there), Tang Dynasty AD 742

E1_seat_rule.question: Are seats spaced by people (one per N), by area (one per A km2), or by a mix?
E1_seat_rule.model: expected seats in a prefecture = c x people^beta x area^(1 - beta); beta = 1 is the map's current people rule, beta = 0 an area rule
E1_seat_rule.fit: on AD 2 only: c for beta = 1 and beta = 0 (Poisson maximum likelihood), and the mixed rule with beta on a 0.05 grid from 0 to 1
E1_seat_rule.data_use: recorded populations and areas (not the Harvest model), prefectures with at least one seat
E1_seat_rule.test: Poisson deviance per prefecture in AD 742, 1102 and 1820 with the AD 2 constants (no refit); also the refitted c per era, reported
E1_seat_rule.decision: the rule with the lowest summed deviance over the three later eras goes to the map's unmarked towns: catchment radius R = sqrt(1 / (pi c' d^beta)) with c' set so that a Han-like density gives the same R as now

E2_held_by_era.question: Does the seats-only extent threshold (5 days for Han AD 2) hold in later eras?
E2_held_by_era.method: the Han window and the v2 monthly graph; inside = the era's prefecture polygons; network = the era's seats; best threshold on the same 1-5 day grid (plus 6, 8, 10), balanced accuracy over land within 15 days of a seat
E2_held_by_era.decision: informative: the map keeps 2 days because its network has roads (Roman test)

E3_riders.question: Does riding put a steppe polity's border with a farming state where it was?
E3_riders.window: a steppe window, centre 41 N 106 E, 4,200 x 2,800 km, 9 km cells
E3_riders.method: the farming state reaches from its seats on foot (v2, twelve months); the steppe polity from every cell of its polygon where the modelled people reach 0.5 per km2, (a) on foot, (b) riding (50 km/day); each cell inside either polygon goes to the faster; balanced accuracy of the assignment
E3_riders.pass: riding (b) above walking (a) in both cases; then riding stays available for the map's lore-named polities as tested
